_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors structure per the international addendum (UAE run — tourism-weighted utilization stack). Sources: abu-dhabi/REVENUE-STACK-ABU-DHABI.md + CREW-COST-ABU-DHABI.md + TOURISM-DEMAND-ABU-DHABI.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-ABU-DHABI.md + SPEED-RULES-ABU-DHABI.md + GEOMETRY-ABU-DHABI.json. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals; the tourism experience layer is the headline layer per the international addendum. All scenario figures transcribed exactly from the worked revenue model and re-verified by script before writing. Demand pools are sourced visitor/attraction flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced Abu Dhabi fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned against Abu Dhabi's operating water-leisure market: sightseeing tours published at US$40–79 per person, and island day-resort passes that bundle the water transfer at AED 480–550 per person. Published hourly charter rates above the small-craft tier are thin, so the charter band is a derived range with a conservative haircut.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor and attraction flows, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect Abu Dhabi's published waterway speed limits — codified rules for facilities, bridges, channels and open water, including a 20-knot cap on all waters after sunset. Evening times are shown at the night cap. Purpose-based relief in no-wake and mangrove waters appears only as a separately labeled layer, never in base times.

fn5.text: Committed-seat and spot pricing is a derived band, not an Abu Dhabi quote: anchored to the published street-taxi tariff and metered cross-city fares, peak road-toll crossings, congestion and travel-time evidence, and the subsidized leisure water-taxi floor. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a UAE-adapted method: published UAE maritime wage surveys for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), plus explicitly stated housing, transport, end-of-service, visa and medical allowances. The model uses $30 per hour loaded — the mid benchmark rounded up as a buffer.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes deliberately thin fills and pays back in about 24 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on sheltered island waters. June–September heat shifts midday leisure sailings toward morning and evening slots; winter is the event-season peak. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at Abu Dhabi's published commercial electricity tariff plus VAT — about $0.057 per kWh. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 5.2×, and every scenario remains cash-positive.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in UAE dirhams and convert at the pegged rate of 3.6725 dirhams per dollar.

fn12.text: The Zaya Nurai island resort is reported temporarily closed for renovation in 2026. Its jetty renders as network reach with that status stated, and no demand is modeled on it.

fn13.text: Lulu Island has no verified public facility today. It renders as an experience anchor only — a scenic loop marker with no landing assumed and no demand modeled on it.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day, twelve months a year. Committed seats form the schedule spine; tourism experiences and charters are the headline layer that carries the payback, priced against a sightseeing market Abu Dhabi's operators already run on daily schedules.

_internal.structure: utilization_stack per the Dubai v3 lead frame, tourism-weighted per the international addendum: committed bundles → spot seats → experiences & charters (headline layer) → upside lines (sponsorship, overnight cargo, relief) → opex → network share → scenario payback.
_internal.sources: REVENUE-STACK-ABU-DHABI.md (all layers, scenario tables, opex). Crew: CREW-COST-ABU-DHABI.md (UAE-adapted method, LOW $20.87 / MID $27.97, model $30/hr). Energy: ADDC commercial 20 fils/kWh + 5% VAT = 21 fils ÷ 3.6725 = $0.0572/kWh flat (energy lines: 1,965/2,154/2,757 nm × 4.1 kWh/nm × $0.0572 = $461/$505/$646, research-file figures used verbatim).

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity hours × $30/hr: 198/245/300 hrs = $5,940/$7,350/$9,000; rendered as the band.
opex_basis.energy: $461/$505/$646 per scenario; rendered as the band. Sensitivity at $0.30/kWh: line rises ~5.2×; nets stay positive in all scenarios (fn10).
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing: $911/mo PRIMARY — Abu Dhabi Maritime Public Marine Facilities tariff, Rabdan Marina commercial wet berth AED 850/ft/yr × 45 ft × 1.05 VAT = AED 40,163/yr. Cross-check Al Saadiyat AED 750/ft/yr → $804/mo. Utilities metered separately.
opex_basis.insurance: $4,167/mo ($50K/yr placeholder ≈ 2% hull + P&I; UAE-licensed insurer mandatory). Flagged for operator quotes.

_internal.opex_total_note: Opex varies by scenario (crew + energy scale; fixed berth+insurance+maintenance = $11,953/mo): $18,354 / $19,808 / $21,599 — rendered as the conservative-to-upside band. Scenario nets reflect per-scenario opex.

layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED $500/$650/$775 per seat-month = 44 legs × spot × ~0.59 bundle discount ($519/$649/$779 rounded). Anchors: metered taxi Yas/Al Raha↔CBD ≈ AED 60 (primary tariff math, observed AED 60–85); Saadiyat↔CBD ≈ AED 32; Darb AED 4/peak crossing; subsidized water-taxi floor AED 10 (leisure schedule, not a commute product); TomTom 29.6% congestion / 57 hrs/yr lost. Band sits below Dubai's derived band, consistent with cheaper road substitutes; ~70–108% of the AED 2,640/mo road-commute anchor. Status everywhere: modeled + fn5. Needs confirmation before external quoting.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $20/$25/$30 per leg × 10/20/30% fill of residual seat-legs (2,464/2,112/1,936). Seats rounded to whole seats (246/422/581); seat count × fare is the exact line (fn7). Note: upside 1,936 × 30% = 580.8 renders 581 per the research file (rounded, not floored).
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $40/$50/$60 pp vs sourced AD sightseeing band US$40.59–78.70 pp (Klook / GetYourGuide / operator pages, live 2025–26); Nurai day pass AED 480–550 pp bundling the water transfer is ceiling context only. Charters $450/$525/$600 per hr — DERIVED with a conservative haircut from the Dubai adjacent-market band ($500–650); local published hourly market above the small-craft tier (~AED 600–700/hr ≈ $163–190) is thin. Weakest-anchored price in this file — flagged.
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder ÷ 4 vessels = $3,125/mo, program precedent. Upside only.
layer_pricing_basis.overnight_cargo_U2: 16 runs × $300 — courier-linehaul rate logic; no AD waterborne freight tariff found ⇒ upside-only. Clean classes per the stack: medical/lab specimens, premium parcels, island-resort resupply (Saadiyat/Yas/Nurai).

_internal.scenario_qa: Mid ~5.5 yr is the honest headline. Conservative is cash-positive but slow (23.8 yr) — rendered with fn8 floor language. Upside 2.4 yr sits at the program's partner-corridor benchmark (2.49 yr) — noted internally only; cross-city comparisons never render.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.label: Energy
tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the multi-city network is the residual-value story.
